decisions.executionNote: Raise and orient both open grippers toward their respective support blocks, keeping elbow-up continuity. Initial block depth is estimated from calibrated head RGB.
Align to the two nearer white supports and descend with open grippers. Wrist views will refine the fingertip alignment before closing.
Use wrist RGB to center each white block between the open fingers; right block needs a larger lateral and downward correction.
Finish small wrist alignment, close both grippers fully on the supports, then lift a short distance to inspect retention.
Both blocks remain between the fingers after the lift. Transport them to symmetric lower-support positions and remove their yaw, keeping both grippers closed.
Lower both retained supports vertically toward the tabletop, maintaining their upright orientation and symmetric spacing.
Set down and release the two lower supports, then lift and separate the open hands without disturbing them.
Both released supports appear upright and symmetric. Reorient the open hands above the long board's ends for a coordinated two-arm grasp.
Replan from the interrupted pose with half-sized rotation increments, completing the board-end approach while preserving joint continuity.
Approach the long board's two ends with open fingers, using small synchronized inward/downward steps and a slight wrist-image centering correction.
Close both grippers around the long board's ends and lift together. Keep the board level and verify retention from both wrist views before translating.
Transport the retained long board forward over the two upright supports, with a small extra lift for clearance and synchronized level motion.
Lower the long board onto both supports and open the grippers while holding position. Inspect seating and centering before retreating.
The lower board appears seated across both supports. Withdraw the open hands upward and outward, then begin reorienting for the remaining white blocks.
Reorient above the two remaining white blocks, matching their visible yaw while staying clear of the completed lower board. Refine alignment from the next wrist images.
Descend with both grippers open and apply small wrist-image centering and yaw corrections to the remaining supports; stop to inspect before closing.
Left approach is obstructed near the lower board; lift and steepen that wrist to approach the back block with more clearance. Make a small final alignment of the right gripper.
Close and test-lift the right support. Refine the steeper left approach with a small backward/downward motion, keeping the lower layer undisturbed.
Avoid further left descent against the nearby board; try a high grasp and short test lift. Raise the visibly retained right support to clearance height.
Both supports appear retained. Lift clear of the lower board and square their yaw without changing the different grasp pitches.
Carry the two retained blocks over the lower board to symmetric middle-support locations, keeping clearance and their upright orientation.
Lower each middle support vertically to the lower board, accounting for the higher left grasp and keeping both blocks upright.
Release the middle supports on the lower board, then withdraw both open grippers upward and outward to inspect their stability.
The released middle supports appear upright. Move back toward the shorter board and gradually turn the open grippers toward its ends.
Finish the gradual board-end wrist rotation and approach above the short board with both grippers open.
Bring the open fingertips down and inward to the short board's ends with a small depth-centering correction from the wrist views.
Complete the short-board end alignment, close both grippers fully, and lift together to verify a level two-handed grasp.
The short board remains between both grippers. Raise it above the middle supports before beginning the level forward transport.
Translate the level short board over the two middle supports while maintaining clearance and closed grippers.
Seat the middle board gently on both upright supports, then open both grippers without moving laterally.
Withdraw from the seated middle board and separate the open hands toward the two remaining top pieces, keeping clear of the tower.
Approach above the brown top board with the left hand and above the green roof piece with the right. Continue gradual orientation changes and inspect wrist alignment.
Refine both top-piece approaches from wrist RGB. Turn and steepen the left grasp toward the brown board, and descend the right hand toward the roof piece with a small lateral correction.
Center the brown board between the left fingers and refine the roof's lateral/yaw alignment in the right wrist view before closing.
The brown board shifted during contact; lift and realign its yaw instead of pushing farther. Center and close the right gripper on the roof piece.
Test-lift the roof with the right gripper closed. Finish the brown board's yaw/centering adjustment and descend carefully for a left-hand grasp.
Close the left gripper on the centered brown board and perform a short vertical test lift. Raise the retained roof safely while waiting for the top board placement.
Both top pieces remain held after lifting. Raise the brown board above the tower and rotate it toward horizontal alignment; bring the roof inward to a clear waiting position.
Carry the retained brown board above the center of the middle layer and finish squaring its long axis. Keep the roof stationary and clear on the right.
Lower the centered brown board vertically toward the middle board. Keep the roof held at a safe waiting position until the brown board is released.
Release the seated brown board and withdraw the left hand. Once clear, carry the held roof inward above the tower without descending yet.
Align the roof over the brown board using head and wrist views, then begin vertical descent. Move the empty left hand farther clear.
Set the roof onto the centered brown board, open the right gripper, and begin a small retreat. Start returning the empty left arm toward origin with gradual rotation.
The released roof appears seated upright. Withdraw the open right hand clear of the tower and continue a gradual, configuration-continuous return toward origin.
All eight pieces appear upright in the tower. Return the left hand to origin and continue the right hand's smooth return, with both grippers open.
Settle the left arm at origin and continue returning the right arm with small pose increments. The released tower remains visually stable.
